rank_five.status: imported upstream theorem, not proved here

golden_ladder.status: imported upstream selection, not derived here
golden_ladder.source: SVD of the rank-five Majorana projection

checks.name: Chiral contraction
checks.constructs: q^T C_chi q with symbolic q

lemmas.claim: q^T C_chi q == xi*eta for symbolic q

checks.proves: the chiral form extracts exactly the product xi*eta for every q: the invariant is a contraction, not a definition
checks.does_not_prove: the value of xi*eta, fixed by the lock-in surface
checks.failure_mode: C_chi mis-transcribed, or contraction != product for symbolic q

checks.name: Boundary metric from the SVD
checks.constructs: spec(P^dag P), P = Sigma V^T with V orthogonal

lemmas.claim: spec(K_Pi) == {phi^-2k}, independent of the basis V

checks.proves: K_Pi = P^dag P has the squared ladder as spectrum, and that spectrum does not depend on the basis V
checks.does_not_prove: that the singular values ARE the golden ladder: that is the upstream selection theorem
checks.failure_mode: spectrum depending on V, or differing from {phi^-2k}

checks.name: Boundary filter and all-pass cell
checks.constructs: pole(H_Pi), P_4(pole), U_eta = M_eta D M_eta^-1

lemmas.claim: numerator P_4 != 0 at the pole (no cancellation)
char poly of U_eta == char poly of D_alpha (isospectral)

checks.proves: the denominator vanishes at 20 phi^4 and the numerator does NOT vanish there, so the pole is not cancelled; the cell U_eta = M_eta D_alpha M_eta^-1 is explicitly constructed and isospectral to D_alpha
checks.does_not_prove: that a single-pole completion is physically necessary. Note also that with the monograph's scalar D_alpha the conjugation is trivially equal, so the content here is the explicit construction and the absence of pole-zero cancellation, not a non-trivial similarity
checks.failure_mode: pole-zero cancellation, or a similarity asserted without constructing the conjugate

checks.name: Pincherle dilatation residue
checks.constructs: Lambda_Pi = 2 phi^2 sqrt5, then its square
checks.proves: kappa == sqrt5, the three forms of Lambda_Pi coincide, and its square equals 20 phi^4
checks.does_not_prove: that the dilatation invariant must be squared: that is the boundary-observable argument
checks.failure_mode: Lambda_Pi mis-transcribed, or the square not closing

checks.name: Fibonacci norm in Z[sqrt5]

lemmas.claim: c^T G c == a^2 + 5b^2 + 2ab sqrt5 for symbolic (a,b)

checks.proves: the quadratic form expands as declared for symbolic (a,b), and on the Fibonacci pair evaluates to 70 + 30 sqrt5 == 20 phi^4
checks.does_not_prove: why the coefficient vector is the Fibonacci pair: that is fixed upstream by the rank-five selection
checks.failure_mode: G mis-transcribed, or the pair not closing

checks.name: Regular matrix representation
checks.constructs: M_Pi, then M_Pi^2 and eval_sqrt5 of it
checks.proves: M_Pi is integral with tr = 2r and det = F5^2 - 5F4^2 = -20; M_Pi^2 is the regular representation of an element of Z[sqrt5] whose evaluation is 20 phi^4
checks.failure_mode: M_Pi^2 not of the form [[a,5b],[b,a]], or eval not closing

checks.name: Chiral tensor anisotropy

lemmas.claim: constructed point lies on the lock-in surface: xi* eta* == a_Pi

checks.proves: the lock-in point built FROM the invariant satisfies xi* eta* == a_Pi and reproduces the anisotropy 11/5: the ratio is derived from the construction, not asserted
checks.does_not_prove: the multiplicities 11 and 5 themselves, which come from the B13 decomposition upstream
checks.failure_mode: the constructed point off the lock-in surface, or the ratio differing from 11/5

checks.name: Filter decomposition B13 = S5 + T8
checks.constructs: S = F_r, T = F_(r+1), B = S + T
checks.proves: the decomposition is dimensionally consistent and its summands are the consecutive Fibonacci numbers straddling the rank
checks.does_not_prove: that the boundary algebra must decompose this way
checks.failure_mode: summands failing to be F_r and F_{r+1}

checks.name: FMT zero mode: non-closure
checks.constructs: f_gain and delta_F from the FMT closure condition
checks.proves: the loop-gain identity f_gain == 1/(1 - delta_F) exactly, and gives a high-precision numerical witness that delta_F != 0
checks.does_not_prove: the transcendence theorem. Rigorous non-vanishing of delta_F rests on Lindemann-Weierstrass, cited and not re-proved here; the numerical test is a witness at the declared precision, not a proof
checks.failure_mode: the gain identity failing, or delta_F vanishing at the declared precision
